name: llmc_layernorm_backward
goal: Port layernorm_backward_harness.cu (llm.c dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu, fp32 build) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers. Keep every kernel variant k in [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10] as its own SYCL kernel, computed on the SYCL device, and keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <input> <output> B T C` reads the inputs and writes each variant's outputs in order as raw float32, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output (atol 0.5 + rtol FLT_EPSILON*|ref|, llm.c's own fp32 rule). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: migrate's output under migrated/ counts, so delete it (delete_file) once your own port is done. migrate's output can be long: read it in parts (read_file offset/limit) or work from the CUDA harness.

museport.note: B=2,T=256 (llm.c: B=8,T=1024); C=1024 (llm.c: C=1600) to keep B*T*C ~0.5M (~2MB) and satisfy C%(32*x128::size)==0 (256 with BF16 x128::size=8) required by kernels 8/9; mean/rstd computed in host_prep from inp via forward formula (llm.c uses layernorm_forward_cpu) and copied to device in gpu_prelude with scratch sized as in llm.c main; tol 0.5 matches dweight/dbias BF16 threshold (dinp 1e-1); kernel1 dropped.
